thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: HIGH_LATENCY on cont-batch streaming path (p95 spike > 700ms, p99 > 2.8s) -- prod us-west-2. Affected service: streaming-infer.

mali: saw the bot. I'm oncall. I'm seeing a sustained p99 ↑ starting ~10:03 UTC, correlates with a big shift in request mix (long prompts + more streaming clients).

ryan: +1, graphs show cont-batch tail grows when mixed-seqlen ratio > 0.35. KV cache churn also increased.

li: can we confirm customer impact? any user-facing error spikes or increased timeouts?

mali: no 5xx increase, just timeouts for streaming clients hitting 30s. A few customers reported slow responses via support ticket (CID 8921). Slackting Sajal for customer comms.

sajal: on it. I'll draft a status note if we need to escalate.

mali: initial triage - looks like continuous batching scheduler is building large heterogeneous batches; preemptive scheduling is deferring mixed short+long sequences and streaming lanes see head-of-line waits. The scheduler fairness metric (fair_share_drift) jumped.

eng-sre: adding logs from a sample worker:

```
2026-03-15T10:04:22Z worker-34 scheduling: batch_size=64 seqlen_dist=[1:0.44, 128:0.28, 512:0.12, 2048:0.16]
2026-03-15T10:04:22Z worker-34 queuing: streaming_slots=0 preempt_count=12 kv_cache_miss=0.37
2026-03-15T10:04:23Z runtime: applied_preemptive_shed=true target_latency_ms=300
```

ryan: runtime is preemptively shedding to protect latency SLO but the aggressive preemptive policy combined with large packing causes streaming stalls. We should consider temporary relax of pack size and enable hedging for streaming.

mali: agree. Proposed live mitigations (quick):
- reduce max_cont_batch_size from 64 -> 32 (fast deploy via ops-bot)
- increase streaming_priority weight by 2x in routing policy
- enable streaming-hedge (send backup replica request at 150ms) for affected routes
- temporary disable cross-pool packing for us-west-2 nodes

li: is reducing batch size going to spike cost? yes but customers > availability. Also impacts throughput. We'll call it a short window.

ops-bot: roll plan draft:
```
- patch: config/max_cont_batch_size = 32
- patch: routing/streaming_priority = +2
- patch: hedging/streaming_backup_ms = 150
- target: us-west-2 pool ids: pool-w2-a/b
- rollout: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% (5m between steps)
- rollback: revert config, restore packer
```

mali: start canary now on pool-w2-a 5%. Ryan please monitor p95/p99 and KV miss. Sajal handle customer comms post-stabilization.

ryan: starting canary deploy 10:06 UTC to pool-w2-a (5%). Watching metrics.

(2m later)

ryan: canary looks promising: p95 dropped from 720ms -> 210ms, p99 from 2.8s -> 680ms. Streaming stalls reduced. KV miss unchanged.

mali: good. proceed to 25% -> 100% with 5m windows.

ops-bot: rolling to 25% at 10:12 UTC.

(5m)

ryan: 25% steady. p95 ~190ms, p99 ~640ms. No regressions on short non-streaming jobs.

mali: roll to 100%.

ops-bot: rolling to 100% at 10:18 UTC.

(6m)

ryan: after full rollout, system stabilized. p95 ~170ms, p99 ~450-600ms (still a bit high but under SLO target of 700ms). Streaming latency improved dramatically.

mali: followup actions (postmortem baked into runbook):
- investigate scheduler heuristics that allow large mixed batches when streaming lanes starve (candidate: prefer homogenous pack thresholds per cycle)
- add adaptive pack_size bound based on live seqlen variance metric
- better KV cache eviction tuning for mixedlen workloads (reduce churn)
- add alert on fair_share_drift > 0.25 earlier (so we don't wait for p99 breach)
- add automated hedging toggle for streaming heavy windows

li: I'll own the post-incident PR for scheduling heuristics. Targeting patch in next sprint plus monitoring.

sajal: customer note: sent proactive message to affected customers, offered SLA credit triage if they'd like. No escalations yet.

mali: incident declared resolved at 10:29 UTC. We'll file a postmortem and link runbook updates here. Thanks all. :tada: 

eng-sre: filing incident doc -> /incidents/6147778888-mixedlen-hedge.json

IncidentBot: Incident resolved (6147778888) 

mali: archive this thread once postmortem is up.

ryan: +1. saved charts and logs to the incident folder.

sajal: closing customer loop later today.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from ryan, :party-parrot: from mali)
